learn.title: Hydrogen Fuel Cells Explained
learn.intro: Hydrogen fuel cells transform clean hydrogen into electricity for zero-emission vehicles, offering a promising alternative to fossil fuels in transportation. Discover how this technology works and its role in decarbonizing mobility.
learn.c1_text: Fuel cells combine hydrogen and oxygen through electrochemical reactions to produce electricity, water, and heat. Like a battery that never runs out, they continuously generate power as long as hydrogen is supplied, making them ideal for long-distance travel.
learn.c2_text: In cars and buses, fuel cells provide steady power without combustion. They operate efficiently at 40-60% efficiency, compared to 20-30% for internal combustion engines. Germany's 15,000 hydrogen trucks demonstrate scalability for heavy transport sectors.
learn.c3_text: India's National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 5 MW electrolyzer capacity by 2026, with plans for 100,000 fuel cell vehicles by 2030. Gujarat and Tamil Nadu are developing hydrogen corridors for public transport and industrial use.
learn.stat2: Fuel cells emit only water vapor during operation
learn.stat4: India's green hydrogen production cost reduced to $3.5/kg (2024)

learn.title: Green Bonds for Climate Finance
learn.intro: Green bonds unlock trillions in capital for renewable energy projects worldwide, channeling investor funds into sustainable infrastructure. Learn how these financial instruments accelerate the clean energy transition through responsible investment.
learn.c1_text: Green bonds are debt securities funding environmental projects like wind farms and solar plants. Investors receive returns while supporting climate action. The World Bank issued $12 billion in green bonds in 2023 alone, setting global standards for transparency.
learn.c2_text: These bonds finance specific clean energy initiatives with strict eligibility criteria. The European Investment Bank's $25 billion green bond portfolio has funded 1,200 renewable projects across 40 countries, demonstrating measurable climate impact through verified outcomes.
learn.c3_text: India issued $5.5 billion in sovereign green bonds in 2023 for solar parks and electric mobility. The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) raised $1.5 billion for rural renewable microgrids, supporting 50,000 solar pumps across states like Maharashtra and Gujarat.
learn.stat2: Global green bond market reached $600 billion (2023)
learn.stat3: World Bank green bonds total $12 billion (2023)
learn.stat4: NABARD raised $1.5 billion for rural solar microgrids

learn.title: Geothermal Energy Fundamentals
learn.intro: Geothermal energy harnesses Earth's natural heat for clean electricity and direct heating, providing baseload power 24/7. Explore how this reliable resource reduces carbon emissions and enhances energy security globally.
learn.c1_text: Geothermal systems tap into hot underground water and rock formations. The US Geological Survey identifies 100,000 MW of technical potential in the western US alone. Like a natural hot water heater, it provides constant energy unlike solar or wind.
learn.c2_text: High-pressure geothermal reservoirs drive turbines through steam or hot water extraction. Enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) create new reservoirs in dry rock using hydraulic fracturing, similar to oil drilling but for energy. Iceland generates 25% of its electricity this way.
learn.c3_text: India's Department of Geothermal Energy targets 5 GW geothermal capacity by 2030, focusing on the Himalayan region and Andaman Islands. The 100 MW Dhankuta project in Nepal supplies clean power to 100,000 households, with India planning cross-border renewable energy corridors.

learn.title: Offshore Wind Farm Development
learn.intro: Offshore wind farms harness powerful ocean winds through sophisticated engineering and grid integration, becoming a cornerstone of Europe's and Asia's renewable energy strategies. Learn about their design, installation, and role in decarbonization.
learn.c1_text: Turbines are mounted on monopiles or floating platforms in waters up to 50m deep. The UK's Dogger Bank project uses 277 turbines generating 1.4 GW, enough for 14 million homes. Installation vessels transport components across oceans, requiring precise engineering in harsh marine conditions.
learn.c2_text: Subsea cables transmit power to onshore substations, often requiring converter stations for AC/DC conversion. Denmark's Horns Rev 3 farm connects via 110 km cable system, converting 407 MW. IRENA notes 150 GW offshore wind globally in 2023, with China leading installations.
learn.c3_text: India's 300 MW Tamil Nadu offshore wind project near Chennai will use floating turbines in 30m depth waters. The Kutch offshore zone in Gujarat offers 50 GW potential. Adani Green Energy partnered with Norway's Equinor for 2 GW projects, targeting 30 GW offshore capacity by 2030.
learn.stat2: UK Dogger Bank: 1.4 GW offshore capacity
learn.stat4: India targets 30 GW offshore wind by 2030

learn.title: Climate Finance & COP Agreements
learn.intro: Climate finance mechanisms and COP agreements channel funds to developing nations for renewable energy transitions, addressing global inequities in climate action. Understand how international commitments translate into tangible clean energy investments.
learn.c1_text: COP27 established the Loss and Damage fund, while COP26 reinforced the $100 billion annual goal for developing nations. The Green Climate Fund has disbursed $14 billion for clean energy projects, including India's solar microgrids in Rajasthan and solar pumps in Punjab.
learn.c2_text: IEA's World Energy Outlook 2024 projects $4.5 trillion annual investment needed for net zero by 2050. Developed nations must triple climate finance to $300 billion yearly. India's 500 GW renewable target requires $1.2 trillion, with 40% needing international support according to IEA analysis.
learn.c3_text: India contributes $2.5 billion annually to the Green Climate Fund and seeks $20 billion in climate finance for its 2070 net zero commitment. The $2.5 billion Solar Parks Scheme, funded partly through climate bonds, enabled 25 GW of solar infrastructure across 25 states since 2015.
learn.stat3: Green Climate Fund disbursed $14 billion for clean energy
learn.stat4: India's 500 GW renewable target requires $1.2 trillion

learn.title: The Duck Curve Challenge
learn.intro: The duck curve describes the steep evening ramp in electricity demand when solar generation drops at sunset, straining grid stability. Discover solutions to manage this solar-induced challenge and ensure reliable power supply.
learn.c1_text: Solar output plummets 50-70% between 4-8 PM as clouds cover panels and sunset approaches. California's grid operator CAISO manages a 12,000 MW evening ramp, equivalent to 12 coal plants. This sudden drop creates grid instability requiring fast-ramping backup power.
learn.c2_text: Battery storage, demand response, and flexible generation address the curve. Australia's Hornsdale Power Reserve (150 MW/193.5 MWh) provides 15 minutes of emergency backup. The US DOE recommends 8-hour storage for daily cycling and hydrogen for seasonal storage to smooth supply-demand gaps.
learn.c3_text: India faces a 10,000 MW evening ramp with 500 GW renewable target. The 10 GW/20 GWh energy storage mission includes pumped hydro and batteries. States like Rajasthan deploy 1,000 MW hybrid projects combining solar-wind-storage, while Telangana uses AI-driven demand response for 500 MW peak shaving.
learn.stat4: India's 10 GW/20 GWh storage mission launched
